description: A web app for astronaut health on long missions. Astronauts click a rotatable 3D body to log symptoms, vitals and moods like stress. The app compares entries to their personal baseline using statistics and machine learning, then gives an explainable readiness advisory (Ready, Caution, Rest) with reasons. A human confirms every decision. An adherence score rewards honest logging and exercise, feeding a post-mission summary. Works offline; uses NASA or synthetic data. Not a medical device.
summary: We developed an AI-powered smart health monitoring application and web platform designed for astronauts aboard spacecraft and space stations. Space environments expose crews to cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, respiratory, and radiation risks, while extreme physical distance prevents routine examinations and forces reliance on fragmented devices and delayed Earth-based medical teams. Our unified system addresses this challenge by connecting to onboard sensors and wearable to continuously track heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, blood temperature, blood sugar, sleep periods, and mood without requiring astronaut intervention. Using artificial intelligence, the platform analyzes vital signs to detect abnormal changes, predict potential health risks, issue immediate alerts, and provide preliminary medical guidance. This solution is vital because it grants astronauts true medical autonomy, enabling early detection and faster emergency responses when immediate intervention from physicians on Earth is not possible.
details: Nova_Med is an autonomous, offline-capable smart medical monitoring and decision-support application designed to protect astronauts aboard spacecraft and space stations without relying on real-time intervention from Earth-based medical teams. Unlike existing fragmented spaceflight solutions—such as single-purpose wearables, the Onboard Diagnostic Kit (ODK), and the Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) that require manual intervention or ground-control assessment—Nova_Med unifies continuous biometric monitoring and AI-driven clinical triage into a single onboard platform. It connects to sensors and wearable devices to track Heart Rate (HR), Blood Pressure (BP), Blood Temperature, Blood Sugar, Respiratory Rate (RR), Sleep periods, and Mood, evaluating incoming readings against space-calibrated clinical baselines to detect abnormal changes early, predict potential health risks, issue immediate alerts, and deliver preliminary medical guidance during communication blackouts. Built by team Hexcoders using JavaScript on the Node.js runtime with a modular Model-View-Controller (MVC) REST API architecture, SQL via an embedded SQLite database (with node-gyp and prebuild-install), structured JSON datasets, Markdown clinical protocols, dotenv, nodemon, and Git, the platform embeds an offline aerospace knowledge base covering 20 specialized protocols (including Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome, decompression sickness, bone loss, muscle atrophy, space radiation, and cardiac emergencies), anatomical body maps, medication references, and radiation dose models. By delivering continuous monitoring, early anomaly detection, faster emergency response, and complete medical autonomy, Nova_Med reduces cognitive load under stress and bridges the medical autonomy gap required for long-duration Lunar and Mars missions while remaining adaptable to remote, offline environments on Earth.
